newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan traders still talking to Yemen on Q4 Masila.
newsitem.headline: Japan traders still talking to Yemen on Q4 Masila.

text.p: Some term lifters for Yemen's Masila crude said on Friday they had yet to reach an agreement on the fourth-quarter price with the oil producer.

Earlier this week, Yemen revised down the price of its Masila crude for the fourth quarter by 10 cents to dated Brent minus 55 cents. This was the level of some bids placed earlier in the negotiations.
A few traders appear to have accepted the offer, traders said.
Other negotiators, however, continued to maintain that the price was too high.
Traders said some negotiators had placed counter bids as low as dated Brent minus 70 cents and minus 90 cents, although the figures could not be confirmed with the parties involved.
The most recent sales of Masila crude in the spot market have been at steep discounts of up to 15 cents to the official selling price.
Traders said Masila crude is difficult to sell in Asia because the price is linked to Brent and not crudes such as Oman and Dubai, which are regarded as benchmarks in Asia.
Brent-linked crudes lose price competitiveness in Asia when the price of Brent rises in comparison with Oman and Dubai.
